source_notes.claim: Men know when they have an STI because symptoms appear.
source_notes.assessment: Many STIs can be asymptomatic; testing is required to determine status.

source_notes.claim: HIV is no longer a death sentence and only requires medicine.
source_notes.assessment: Effective antiretroviral therapy can support long, healthy lives, but HIV remains a chronic infection requiring ongoing care and prevention.

source_notes.claim: Young children only understand physical punishment.
source_notes.assessment: The episode offers this as opinion; major pediatric guidance advises against spanking and harsh physical punishment.

source_notes.claim: Police could have sex with sex workers in Hawaii.
source_notes.assessment: This is disputed in the room and must be treated as an unverified historical/legal claim, not a present rule.

source_notes.claim: Holding someone's head prevents them turning away from a kiss.
source_notes.assessment: Physical technique cannot substitute for freely given present consent; a turned face and repeated no are boundaries.

source_notes.claim: A paid month-long girlfriend experience can be a human experiment if both people know generally.
source_notes.assessment: The proposal lacks worker terms, independent consent, labor protections, privacy controls and publication revocation; it is not research or an agreed project.
